content:
Maria L.: FYI — after the continuous-batcher heuristic roll yesterday we got a P95 uplift on small-prefix requests in us-east-1-g8x. Not huge (200–350ms) but consistent for ~30m.
Devon: saw the same in prod dashboards, mostly 1-3 token prefix hits. any kernel affinity changes in the rollout?
Ajay: no kernel changes in the config. the heuristic tweak lowered token_budget_target for short sequences and merged more aggressively across queues.
Kevin: grabbed a trace — kv shard unlock spikes line up with batch flushes. attaching a quick snippet from the trace:
```
[2026-03-17T13:12:45Z] kv_cache.cpp:unlock_shard shard=7 held_us=12543 requester=batcher-127
[2026-03-17T13:12:45Z] batcher.cpp:complete_batch batch_id=127 tokens=42 dispatch_ms=2
[2026-03-17T13:12:45Z] kernel_dispatch.cpp:dispatch finish_us=1605523160450 queue_wait_us=183
[2026-03-17T13:12:45Z] kv_cache.cpp:unlock_shard shard=3 held_us=9802 requester=batcher-128
```
Kevin: those held_us numbers are an order of magnitude above baseline. looks like shard-level locking is getting contended when lots of tiny batches finish concurrently.
Tera: could be microburst unlock storms — continuous-batcher merging candidates across many queues so many shards touched at near-same-time.
Ajay: hypothesis: lowering token_budget_target increased flush frequency for small requests -> more batch terminations -> more KV unlock events clustered. that would amplify lock contention on hot prefix shards.
Devon: can we repro with the loadtester? run 10k rps of 20–60 token reqs and capture kv histograms.
Maria L.: yes please. Kevin, crater a short perf job with the new heuristic config and the previous one (2.6) side-by-side. include per-shard lock_hold_us histogram.
Kevin: running now. quick command I used locally: `./bin/loadtest --profile small-prefix --qps 8k --duration 10m --flags continuous_batcher.token_budget=6`
Kevin: initial run shows per-shard p99 lock_hold_us ~12ms under new heuristic vs ~0.9ms under 2.6. throughput also slightly lower (-4%) when contended.
Ajay: that matches theory. simple mitigation options: 1) increase per-shard backoff/queue jitter on unlock, 2) raise token_budget_target for small sequences, 3) stagger batch completion with tiny random delay.
Tera: prefer option 1 + 2. jitter introduces tail jitter risk for latency-sensitive flows.
Devon: agree. option 1 is low-risk and can be limited to shard hotness heuristics.
Maria L.: since this is affecting prod, please coordinate a rollback for us-east-1-g8x while we ship a fix.
deploy-bot: rollback started — continuous-batcher config reverted to 2.6 for pool us-east-1-g8x at 2026-03-17T13:30:12Z.
Kevin: after rollback P95 returned to baseline within 12m. confirmed via dashboards. I'll attach the csvs to the incident ticket.
Maria L.: great. next actions: Ajay to prototype per-shard unlock backoff (short exponential capped at 5ms) + a conservative bump to token_budget_target for short sequences. Kevin to validate with loadtest and perf traces. Tera/Devon to plan canary.
Ajay: on it. will open a PR with tests and a small perf harness. estimated patch + canary in 48h.
Devon: can we also add a kv unlock metric (histogram) to the console per-pool? would help future debugging.
Maria L.: yes please. make that a part of the rollout checklist for batching heuristic changes. thanks all :thumbsup:
